decision.title: Arrays and function items (packet )
decision.summary: Arrays are AVL trees of cells updated by split and join in O(log n); function items need a registered function type; maps and arrays act as functions through stateless bodies.

item.p: Arrays are AVL trees of cells (one cell class): a flat node holds members inline (sxml_array_make, so get is O(1)); a run node names a part of a flat node's members (splitting a leaf copies nothing); a branch node joins two subtrees. The array item's cell is the root; the empty array is a flat node of no members. Every update is split plus join (Blelloch et al., "Just Join", without middle keys): append, put, insert, remove and slice are O(log n), get O(log n). 10^5 appends are tested at most 1 + 3 x height allocations each; deep nesting frees through the pending list.

Function items: the signature must be a registered function type other than function(*) (arity = its parameter count), else INVALID_ARGUMENT. Annotations are kept as the borrowed view; captured values are retained; the body's runs once on make and once when the cell is freed.

Maps and arrays as functions: sxml_function_item_describe gives a stateless static body (map:get through sxml_map_find, array:get with 1-based positions). The bodies check their argument although coercion is the caller's: not one atomic key / one integer is XPTY0004; a position out of range, also beyond int64_t, is FOAY0001.
